newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt says 1997 Q1 CPI (A) up 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: HK govt says 1997 Q1 CPI (A) up 6.2 pct.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Friday the Consumer Price Index (A) rose by 6.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997 against 5.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996 and 6.0 percent in the fourth quarter.
The composite CPI increased by 6.1 percent in the first quarter of 1997, compared to 5.7 percent in the third quarter of 1996 and 6.1 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.

"There was nevertheless some deceleration in inflation within the first quarter of 1997. On a year-on-year comparison, the CPI (A) rose by 6.6 percent in January, 6.5 percent in February and 5.7 percent in March," the government said in its First Quarter Economic Report 1997.

The GDP deflator as a broad measure of overall inflation in the economy was 6.2 percent higher in the fourth quarter of 1996 than a year earlier. This compared with an increase of 5.2 percent in the first half of the year, and 4.8 percent in the third quarter.
The composite CPI is made up of CPI (A), CPI (B) and the Hang Seng CPI.
